The suspect, 22-year-old Kalin, has an extensive history of traffic violations according to court records.
These include more than seven speeding citations over the past four years,
along with prior street racing citations in August 2025 and in 2023, indicating repeated involvement
in high-speed driving incidents. Records also show that in April 2022, Kaelin was charged with
a misdemeanor for speeding and later found guilty in San Juan County Magistrate Court,
where she was sentenced to 90 days of unsupervised probation. During the investigation,
officers also recovered 13 9mm rounds and a Keltec pistol at the scene. Ownership of both items
was not immediately determined. Kalin was arrested and booked into the San Juan County Detention Center,
where she was charged with racing on highways, a felony offense under New Mexico law. The driver of
the BMW, identified as Reese, was charged with fourth-degree aggravated fleeing a law enforcement
officer, third-degree great bodily injury by vehicle while driving under the influence, driving
without required lighted lamps, and racing on highways. Both suspects remain innocent unless proven
guilty in a court of law.
